verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The Lean takes the same mean-value step in a different shape, and only inside a proof. The paper bounds one mixed component ∂_x^α∂_t^j G, in the time direction only, by |t'-t| times the supremum of the single next time derivative ∂_x^α∂_t^{j+1} G over the compact set K_0×[t,t']. The Lean theorem's statement (GenericEndpointExtension.lean:455-458) is only `UniformContinuousOn (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f) s` — it carries no constant, no increment and no (n+1)-st derivative. The quantitative inequality lives one level down, as the proof step `hLip : LipschitzOnWith K (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f) s` at line 461, whose constant `K = ⟨max C 0, _⟩` (line 460) is internal to the proof: it is a Lipschitz bound on the whole joint jet over an open convex s, for any C bounding ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (n+1) f‖ on all of s, with the displacement measured in the full (t,x) norm rather than |t'-t|. Specialising s to a product neighbourhood and the two points to (t',x) and (t,x) gives a bound of the paper's left side, but with the larger right side |t'-t|·sup_s‖(n+1)-jet‖ in place of |t'-t|·sup_{K_0×[t,t']}|∂_x^α∂_t^{j+1}G|, so the displayed inequality as written is not supplied. The use the paper makes of it — every fixed derivative is uniformly Cauchy as t ↑ 1, so the limits exist — is proved: `actualJet_uniformContinuousOn` feeds `exists_limit_of_uniformContinuousOn` (GenericEndpointExtension.lean:481,488) and then `OffplaneJetExtensions.extension_of_local_jets`, whose docstring records that the endpoint derivative limits are constructed there rather than assumed.
